description: OU parameter fitting from per-wallet wci_series (26-week TCI trajectories)

scientific_connections.S10F_kimura: kappa (OU restoring force) = stabilizing selection strength s (Hansen 1997). Bulk OU = stabilizing selection; tail (kappa≈0) = directional selection = Kimura arms-race regime.
scientific_connections.S43_fdr: OU equilibrium predicts FDR ≈ 1 (sigma²/(2*kappa) = chi_0). Departure from FDR=1 signals tail agents. FluctuationOracleV2 on-chain measures this.
scientific_connections.S48_lagrangian: Kramers escape rate from OU well (§48C) gives theoretical tail fraction. kappa and sigma from data → compute predicted P(escape to Pe>Pe_c). Compare to empirical §50J f_d.
scientific_connections.S50K_ou: Confirms the OU interpretation: bulk kappa>0 (reverting), tail kappa≈0 (non-reverting). The y_K^(temp)=-0.40 result is recovered from OU: Pe(M) ∝ M^{-1/2} for OU trajectories.

interpretation: Bulk crypto traders exhibit Ornstein-Uhlenbeck dynamics with kappa > 0 (mean-reverting to personal TCI baseline). Pareto tail agents have kappa ≈ 0 (non-reverting, directional drift). This is identical to the stabilizing vs directional selection dichotomy in population genetics (§10F Kimura identity). kappa maps to stabilizing selection coefficient s via s = kappa/2. FDR near 1 for bulk agents confirms OU equilibrium (§43 FDR theorem). Kramers escape rate from §48C predicts the empirical tail fraction.
